userStories.title: [OPERATOR] Search Console diagnostic: separate no-demand from no-indexation before any SEO build
userStories.description: As the operator, I want to know which of the three causes is producing zero traffic, so that we do not spend a quarter building content when the real problem is that Google is not indexing what we already shipped.
acceptanceCriteria: Record trailing-90-day impressions, clicks and average position for the four ALREADY-SHIPPED URLs that target real low-competition demand: /compare/mercari-vs-ebay (5,000/mo, competition index 1) and the reseller-glossary pages for 'what does euc mean', 'what does nwt mean' and 'what does pre owned mean' (5,000/mo each, Low).
Record indexed vs 'Crawled - currently not indexed' vs 'Discovered - currently not indexed' counts per sitemap segment, one row per functions/sitemap-*.xml.ts file.
Record total site impressions over 90 days and the average position of every query above 50 impressions.

Write the verdict (cause 1 no-demand / cause 2 no-indexation / cause 3 no-authority) with the supporting numbers into the diagnosis section of vault/40-growth/seo-strategy-options-2026-08.md, and bump its `reviewed` date.

If the verdict is cause 2 or cause 3, append a BLOCKED note to every Path 1, 3 and 7 build story in prd-seo.json naming the blocking cause: no new content universe helps until indexation or authority is fixed.
userStories.notes: DONE 2026-08-18. Search Console export (keyword/, Web, 2026-05-25..2026-08-16) analysed. VERDICT: none of the three causes. Site is 10 weeks into a normal indexation ramp -- 2 impressions/week in early June to 2,410/week by 2026-08-16; 6,434 impressions / 55 clicks / 270 URLs / 366 queries over 6mo. Cause 1 failed (impressions accelerating). Cause 2 failed (270 URLs earning impressions; /sitemap.xml is a flat 519-URL urlset exactly equal to the union of all 15 segment sitemaps, no orphans; the 4 named URLs are 200 + self-canonical + index,follow + in sitemap). Cause 3 failed (156 of 270 URLs in the top 10). REAL CAUSE is a fourth: ranking without clicks -- 149 URLs at position 3-10 convert at 0.85% vs a 3-10% baseline; 'vguc meaning' = 355 impressions at position 8.88 and ZERO clicks. NO BLOCKED notes applied: causes 2 and 3 both failed. Working: docs/seo/US-9001-VERDICT.md. Worklist: docs/seo/ctr-rewrite-worklist.csv (19 URLs). Vault diagnosis section updated, reviewed date already 2026-08-18.

userStories.title: CTR copy pass on the page-one URLs that rank and get skipped
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the pages already ranking on page one to actually earn their clicks, so that we capture the traffic we have before spending a quarter building more of it. US-9001 found 149 URLs at position 3-10 converting at 0.85% against a 3-10% baseline. This is a copy pass over pages that already exist, not a build, and it is the cheapest work in this file.
acceptanceCriteria: Rewrite the title and meta description for the 19 URLs in docs/seo/ctr-rewrite-worklist.csv, working down the clicks_being_missed_6mo column. Fill the proposed_title and proposed_meta_description columns first so the change is reviewable before it ships. DONE, and the CSV now carries a shipped column recording which of the three surfaces each URL landed on.

The top four carry most of the value: /grading/glossary/vguc (503 impressions, position 8.8, 0.20% CTR), /blog/mercari-partial-item-returns-reseller-guide (607, 8.5, 0.82%), /compare/vinted-vs-mercari (530, 8.5, 1.13%) and /value/nike/tech-fleece (116, 6.5, 0.00%). All four rewritten.

Size of the prize is stated honestly in the story and not inflated: closing the entire gap is worth about 66 clicks over six months against the 55 the site earned. It roughly doubles a small number. It is worth a day, and it is not the growth plan. Restated at the top of docs/seo/ctr-rewrite-pass.md.

Titles for definitional pages are rewritten to promise something the SERP snippet cannot deliver. Nineteen glossary pages earn 1,087 impressions and 4 clicks between them because Google answers the definition in place; a title that only restates the definition cannot win the click. DONE for vguc, inr and the glossary hub.

Every rewritten title still satisfies keyword-targets.test.ts, meaning the primary keyword remains in the registered title or description. Only /condition-grading of the 19 carries a KEYWORD_TARGETS entry; its primary (clothing condition grading) opens the new description.

CORRECTED 2026-08-18: the 19 URLs are not one surface and cannot ship in one commit. 11 are PUBLIC_ROUTES entries on a 46-char title budget (the 60-char cap minus the " | GradeThread" suffix), 1 is a Pages Function template with a 60-char budget, and 7 are blog_posts rows whose SERP copy is a database column an admin can also edit. The blog seven need scripts/apply-blog-ctr-rewrites.mjs run against prod; everything else ships with the build.

src/test/ctr-rewrite-worklist.test.ts asserts the shipped registry copy equals the reviewed copy in the CSV, and that every blog proposal fits the SERP budget. The record and the code cannot drift apart silently. DONE, 16 tests.

STILL OPERATOR WORK, BUT THE SCRIPT IS NOW VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, NOT JUST DRY-RUN. Run scripts/apply-blog-ctr-rewrites.mjs --apply with prod credentials for the 7 blog rows. On 2026-08-18 the write path was exercised end to end against the throwaway local stack with a seeded fixture of the seven real slugs, covering all four branches: write, same (idempotent re-run), edited (skipped), and --force (overrides). IT HAD A DEFECT AND WOULD HAVE DAMAGED PROD.

REMAINING (operator): a follow-up Search Console read on 2026-10-17, 60 days after the pass, comparing CTR per URL against the ctr_actual_pct column captured here, with the result recorded against US-9016 threshold table.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-18, before the script ever touched prod. The clobber guard carried a third clause, `post.title === rewrite.currentTitle`, which defeated it in the COMMONEST case: five of the seven rows had seo_title NULL at capture, so current_title WAS title; once an admin set seo_title in the admin UI, title still matched current_title, the clause fired, and the script overwrote the admin's edit while printing 'wrote'. That is the exact thing the script's own header promises never happens. Proven with a seeded row, then fixed.

IT COULD NOT HAVE BEEN CAUGHT ANY OTHER WAY. The dry run never opens a database connection, so it exercises none of the clobber logic; the 16 existing tests all worked on the CSV. This is the repo's own standing lesson (CLAUDE.md: 'Before writing "cannot be verified locally" about anything REST-shaped, try it') holding for the fourth time.

SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT: a row already carrying the PROPOSED title but not the proposed description was reported as 'edited' and skipped, when it is a part-written earlier run and is resumable. The guard now matches the contract its header states, which is 'differs from BOTH current_title and proposed_title'.

THE GUARD IS NOW TESTABLE AND TESTED. isUntouched() was extracted, declared in scripts/apply-blog-ctr-rewrites.d.mts, and covered by 5 new cases in src/test/ctr-rewrite-worklist.test.ts (21 total), including one named for the exact shape that was being clobbered. Note for the next reader: that .d.mts is what tsc reads for this module, NOT the .mjs, so a new export is invisible to the typechecker until it is declared there.
userStories.notes: Script verified against the local stack 2026-08-18 and two defects fixed. Still open on two operator items: the prod --apply, and the 2026-10-17 Search Console follow-up.

userStories.title: Calculator page family: route registry, prerender, JSON-LD and its own sitemap segment
userStories.description: As a reseller searching for a fee or shipping calculator, I want GradeThread's tools to be crawlable, fast-loading pages, so that they can rank and earn links instead of sitting behind the SPA.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/lib/seo/calculators.ts exports calculatorRoutes(): PublicRoute[] and is spread into PUBLIC_ROUTES in src/lib/seo/public-routes.ts, following the pattern of comparisonRoutes() and glossaryRoutes(). DONE.

The registry carries a status flag per calculator. calculatorRoutes() emits only `live` entries, and emits NOTHING AT ALL (hub included) while every entry is planned: an empty list page is a worse result than no page. This makes US-9002 and US-9003 land together by construction. DONE.

When the first calculator goes live: its path and the hub are added to src/prerender/entry-server.tsx (both the PAGES map and the page-module map, which are lockstep-guarded), and src/lib/seo/__tests__/public-routes.test.ts plus the prerender sync-guard pass.

src/prerender/head-builder.ts jsonLdForRoute() emits WebApplication JSON-LD for each live calculator and CollectionPage for the hub, mirrored by the <SEO jsonLd=…> prop on the live SPA route, per the react-helmet-async gotcha in CLAUDE.md. Follow /tools/authenticity-check and /tools/fit-checker, which are already wired at head-builder.ts:198-199.

Each live calculator has a KEYWORD_TARGETS entry in src/lib/seo/keyword-targets.ts; keyword-targets.test.ts passes, meaning the primary keyword appears in the registered title or description. The registry already carries primaryKeyword per entry so the two cannot drift.

CORRECTED 2026-08-18, no sitemap segment file is needed. The original AC asked for functions/sitemap-tools.xml.ts referenced from functions/sitemap.xml.ts. Verified while building: any route in PUBLIC_ROUTES flows into the sitemap manifest automatically and lands in both /sitemap.xml and sitemap-marketing.xml via partitionedStaticUrls() (functions/_shared/sitemap.ts:266). /sitemap.xml only becomes a sitemapindex above SITEMAP_MAX_URLS = 5000 and the site is at 519 URLs, so a tools segment would be a second copy of URLs already advertised, which is what the 15 existing segments already are. Do not build it.

`npm run ui:check` reports zero findings for src/, and `npx tsc -b` is clean. DONE: 12 new tests in src/lib/seo/__tests__/calculators.test.ts, 446 route-guard tests still passing, ui:check at 0 blocking.
userStories.notes: Infrastructure landed 2026-08-18: src/lib/seo/calculators.ts (registry of 8 with a live/planned status flag, hub metadata, breadcrumbs, calculatorRoutes()), wired into public-routes.ts, and src/lib/seo/__tests__/calculators.test.ts (12 tests). Two ACs corrected against the real code: the sitemap segment file is unnecessary (see AC6), and the hub cannot ship before the first calculator. US-9007 flipping measurement-converter to live activated the hub, both prerender maps, both keyword-targets entries and the sitemap entries, which is exactly the by-construction landing this story was designed for. The remaining calculators are separate stories blocked on fee data, not unfinished work here. One defect found afterwards and fixed in the US-9017 commit: calculatorHubJsonLd pointed isPartOf at the Organization node rather than the WebSite node, which entity-graph-jsonld.test.ts was red on.

userStories.title: eBay fee calculator at /tools/ebay-fee-calculator
userStories.description: As an eBay seller working out what a sale will net, I want a fee calculator that handles category final value fees, insertion fees and promoted-listing rates, so that I get the real number instead of a rough guess.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE: computes and itemises the category final value fee, the per-order fixed fee, the seller-standing surcharge, the insertion fee past the free allotment, promoted listings, the international fee and the dispute fee, from sale price, shipping, tax, category, store tier, listing format and standing. Payout and profit fall out of it.

CORRECTED, no effectiveFrom field. The AC asked for one. eBay prints no effective date on either fee page, so an effectiveFrom would be a date we invented, and a made-up freshness stamp is worse than none. src/lib/ebay-fee-schedule.ts carries EBAY_FEES_RETRIEVED_ON instead and the page states it, which is checkable.
DONE: the prerendered HTML is 1,078 words with the full store-tier table, the fee explanation and all five FAQs, before any script runs.
DONE: targets ebay fee calculator as primary with ebay final value fee calculator, how much does ebay take from a sale and ebay seller fees as secondary, all registered in keyword-targets.ts.

DONE: 17 tests in src/lib/__tests__/ebay-fee-schedule.test.ts, every expected number hand-computed in a comment beside it. Includes the free-insertion crossing on an Anchor auction, the handbag cliff where a $2,001 sale costs LESS than a $1,999 one, and the athletic-shoe threshold where the rate drops and the per-order fee stops.

THE SCHEDULE IS THREE SHAPES, not one rate, which is what every naive fee calculator gets wrong. Apparel is MARGINAL (13.6% up to $7,500, then 2.35%). Handbags are a CLIFF (crossing $2,000 re-rates the whole sale). Athletic shoes are CONDITIONAL (at $150 the rate drops AND the per-order fee stops). Starter Store gets no discount at all.

SIDE EFFECT, and the most valuable thing in this story: src/lib/ebay-fees.ts carried 13.25% for apparel. That is a real eBay rate belonging to Coins & Paper Money and the trading cards, not apparel. It is read by ScoutAI buy/skip and by the composer profit estimate, both of which have been understating fees by 0.35 points in the seller favour. Corrected in both copies of the mirror, and in the reader-facing fee figures on 16 comparison pages and the where-to-sell guide.
userStories.notes: SHIPPED 2026-08-18 after the operator confirmed the schedule against eBay own pages (id=4822, id=4809, id=4164). The confirmed sheet is docs/seo/ebay-fee-schedule-CONFIRMED.csv and it corrected nine of the 27 rows plus added twelve that were missing: the Basic-and-above 12.7% tier, the real $7,500/$2,500 thresholds rather than $2,000, the handbag cliff structure, the sub-$150 athletic fallback, per-tier insertion fees, the yearly-versus-monthly store pricing mismatch, the not-as-described surcharge and the $20 dispute fee. Two things the sheet resolved by deleting: there is no separate sneaker rate, and there is no US regulatory operating fee. The one field nobody could supply is the typical promoted-listing ad rate, which is now an input on the page rather than a guessed default. 4,800+ tests green.

userStories.title: eBay shipping calculator at /tools/ebay-shipping-calculator
userStories.description: As a seller pricing a listing, I want to compare shipping cost by weight, dimensions and service, so that I do not lose margin by guessing postage.
acceptanceCriteria: Takes weight, package dimensions, origin and destination ZIP, and returns a compared table of the services a clothing seller actually uses, including a flat-rate versus weight-based recommendation. DONE. Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and the six Priority Mail Flat Rate containers, sorted by price, with a line stating which side wins and by how much.

Rate data is a dated static table with an `effectiveFrom` field, not a live carrier API call, so the page prerenders and cannot break on a third-party outage. DONE. USPS_RATES_EFFECTIVE_FROM is 2026-08-08 and is printed on the page. Zone comes from a packed table of 896 ZIP-prefix centroids built from the Census 2020 ZCTA gazetteer, so even the zone lookup makes no network call.

Dimensional weight is applied and shown as its own line when it exceeds actual weight, since that is the case sellers get wrong. DONE, with the three 2026-07-12 rule changes modelled: divisor 139 (was 166), dimensions rounded up to the whole inch before anything is measured, and the one-cubic-foot floor below which dimensions are ignored entirely.

Targets `ebay shipping calculator` (50,000/mo, Low) as primary and `cheapest way to ship clothes` (500/mo) as secondary, both registered in keyword-targets.ts. DONE, plus two more secondaries and four question targets.

A unit test covers a dimensional-weight case and a flat-rate-cheaper case. DONE, 16 tests in src/lib/__tests__/usps-rate-schedule.test.ts, including the puffer-jacket dim case (2 lb on the scale, billed at 19 lb) and both directions of the flat-rate comparison.

SOURCING, which is the part that took the time: every number was read off a published rate sheet and confirmed against a second independent source before it was allowed into the code. Source A is Pirate Ship's August 8 2026 USPS rate workbook, source B is USPS Notice 123 at pe.usps.com. They agree to the cent on all 20 values checked. The working is in docs/seo/usps-rate-schedule-CONFIRMED.csv, following the rule US-9003 produced after its first draft had 13.25% for apparel.

PRICE TIER IS STATED, not implied. These are USPS commercial prices, the tier an online label buys. eBay's own rates are at or below it, so the page says a result is a ceiling rather than a quote, and says counter prices run 30-40% higher.

THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: Ground Advantage charges ONE price per zone under a pound and it is LOWER than the 1 lb price ($6.93 vs $7.61 in Zone 1). A package crossing 16 oz costs more. That cliff got its own table on the page and its own test, because it is the cheapest thing a clothing seller can act on.

userStories.title: Fee calculators for Poshmark, Mercari, Depop and Etsy
userStories.description: As a seller who lists across several marketplaces, I want the same fee calculator for each of them, so that I can compare what a given item nets on each platform.
acceptanceCriteria: One page per marketplace under /tools/{marketplace}-fee-calculator, generated from the shared calculator family rather than four hand-built pages. DONE. ONE component, src/pages/tools/marketplace-fee-calculator.tsx, parameterised by MarketplaceKey and exported four times. Everything that differs between the platforms is data in the fee schedule or the calculator registry.

Each uses the same dated fee-schedule module shape as the eBay calculator, so a platform rate change is a one-file edit. DONE. src/lib/marketplace-fee-schedules.ts holds all four in one shape: a rate, a base, at most one threshold rule, processing, listing fee, promotion and buyer fee.

A cross-platform comparison view shows the same item's net across all five marketplaces and links to the relevant /compare/ page. DONE, on every one of the four pages, sorted by payout, with the /compare/ link resolved in either direction and omitted when no page exists (Etsy has none, so it shows none rather than linking to a 404).

Targets registered in keyword-targets.ts: `depop fee calculator`, `etsy fee calculator`, `how much does poshmark take`, `poshmark fee calculator` and `mercari fee calculator`. DONE, four entries with three secondaries and three question targets each.

A unit test asserts one worked example per marketplace against hand-computed totals. DONE, 15 tests in src/lib/__tests__/marketplace-fee-schedules.test.ts. All five worked examples pass on the same $40 item with $8 shipping and $3 tax.

SOURCING: every rate was read off the marketplace's OWN fee page and confirmed against a second source before it entered the code. Poshmark from its Posh Guide, Mercari from help_center article 2518, Depop from its Help Centre fee table and its own newsroom announcement, Etsy from Etsy Fee Basics plus the per-country processing table plus the Offsite Ads page. Working in docs/seo/marketplace-fees-CONFIRMED.csv. Third story running this procedure.

EBAY IS NOT DUPLICATED. The comparison row calls calculateEbayFees() from the existing eBay module rather than re-entering its rates, so the table and /tools/ebay-fee-calculator cannot drift apart. A test asserts eBay is the only one of the five charging on sales tax.

THE FINDING: headline rates are not comparable, because the five charge them on five different bases. On a $40 item with $8 shipping and $3 tax, Depop nets $45.87 and Poshmark nets $40.00, a $5.87 spread, and the platform with the LOWEST headline rate (Etsy at 6.5%) finishes third. That comparison is the reason the page exists rather than four separate answers.

userStories.title: Reseller profit calculator that takes CONDITION as an input
userStories.description: As a reseller deciding whether an item is worth listing, I want a profit calculator that factors the item's condition into the estimated sale price, so that I get a realistic number rather than one based on a mint-condition comp.
acceptanceCriteria: Inputs cost of goods, marketplace, sale price, shipping, and a condition grade on the 1.0-10.0 scale; outputs gross, fees, net profit, margin and ROI. DONE. The marketplace selector reuses the US-9005 fee schedules, so all five platforms are priced by the same code the fee calculators use.

The condition input adjusts the estimated sale price using the same tier definitions the grading engine uses, and the page states the adjustment applied rather than hiding it. DONE, and the tier function is now SHARED rather than duplicated: tierLabelForGrade moved out of whats-it-worth.tsx into src/lib/condition-value-curve.ts and both surfaces import it.

TWO grades, not one. The calculator asks what condition the COMP was in as well as the item, because a comp taken from a mint listing overstates a worn item and a comp from a beaten one understates a clean one. Every competing calculator assumes the comp is mint and can only adjust downward, which is why sellers using them under-price good stock.

A 'grade this item' call to action links to the grading flow, and the link carries a PostHog property so the calculator-to-grading path is measurable. DONE. New registry event calculator_grading_cta_click with the {source, destination} property shape already used by comparison_crosslist_cta_click, so US-9010 can read both funnels off one shape.
Targets `reseller profit calculator`, `ebay profit calculator` and `resale profit margin calculator`, registered in keyword-targets.ts. DONE.

A unit test asserts that two identical items differing only in condition grade produce different estimated sale prices, and that a 10.0 grade applies no downward adjustment. DONE, 12 tests in src/lib/__tests__/condition-value-curve.test.ts.

THE MULTIPLIERS ARE MEASURED, NOT INVENTED, which was the real work in this story. They are derived from GradeThread's own public Condition Index: 53 published curves resting on 3,811 eBay sold comps, each grade's median divided by that curve's grade-10 median, then the median of those 53 ratios. scripts/seo/derive-condition-value-curve.mjs re-runs it against live data and reproduces the committed table exactly.

WHAT THE NUMBERS ARE NOT is stated in the module and on the page: each Index curve is anchored on three measured bands of up to 25 comps, and the grades between anchors are the Index's own interpolation. So it summarises 159 measured bands, not 3,811 independent observations of ten grades.

THE SPREAD IS PUBLISHED NEXT TO THE AVERAGE. At grade 9.0 the ratio runs 0.527 to 1.000 across the 53 items, so the page prints the range beside every median and tells the reader to look at it first. When the seller picks a specific Condition Index item, the calculator uses that item's own measured curve and says which of the two it used.
FOLLOW-UP: US-2280 (regress realized FlipDesk outcomes against assigned grades) would replace this derived curve with an outcome-grounded one. The module names it.

userStories.title: Measurement and size converter at /tools/measurement-converter
userStories.description: As either a seller writing measurements or a buyer reading them, I want a converter that handles garment measurements and international sizing, so that I can tell whether an item will fit without guessing.
acceptanceCriteria: Converts between US, UK, EU and JP sizing for women's clothing, men's tops and shoes, and between inches and centimetres for pit to pit, length, sleeve, waist and inseam. DATA DONE in src/lib/size-conversion.ts.

The measurement definitions are READ FROM MEASUREMENT_SPECS (src/lib/measurements.ts), not retyped, so the converter cannot disagree with what MeasureCard collects. A test asserts every label matches, and that the flat-to-worn doubling set agrees with isCircumferenceMeasurement rather than keeping a second list. DONE.

The page leads with the flat-to-worn doubling, not the size tables: a 21 inch pit to pit fits a 42 inch chest, and that misreading costs more sales than any label mismatch. MEASUREMENT_HOWTO carries a how and a pitfall for all 9 measurements.

Every size table renders SIZE_TABLE_CAVEAT next to it. The international tables are approximate by nature (no standards body, vanity sizing moves them a full size) and the page says so rather than implying precision it does not have.

The men's EU column is DERIVED and shown as such (mensChestInchesToEu: chest in cm, halved) rather than presented as folklore. That derivation test caught two rows of the first draft being three sizes adrift at XXL and 3XL.
Targets `international size conversion chart`, `pit to pit measurement chart`, `mens to womens size converter` and `clothing measurement converter`, registered in keyword-targets.ts.
This is the one calculator serving buyers as well as sellers (1,600/mo combined); it links into both the buyer-facing condition glossary and the seller measurement flow.

DONE: the page at /tools/measurement-converter and the hub at /tools/calculators, both prerendered, both with JSON-LD from head-builder.ts, both in the SPA router, keyword-targets entries for both, and the registry entry flipped to live -- which is what activated US-9002's wiring. DONE: two flat-lay diagrams, a top and a pair of trousers, with all nine measurements drawn as labelled tape lines. Picking a measurement in the converter lights up its line and dims the rest, so the diagram answers the question the prose cannot -- front rise and pit to pit are not picturable from a sentence.
userStories.notes: Data layer landed 2026-08-18: src/lib/size-conversion.ts + 25 tests. Chosen as the first calculator to build because it is the ONLY one needing no external rate data -- US-9003 through US-9006 are all blocked on fee schedules. Length conversion is exact; the international tables are approximate and labelled so. OPTIONAL REVIEW: docs/seo/size-tables-to-review.csv has all 28 rows for the operator to check, but nothing is blocked on it. PAGE SHIPPED 2026-08-18. Flipping measurement-converter to live activated the whole family: the hub, the sitemap entries and the prerender all came on with it. 835 tests green, tsc -b clean, ui:check 0 blocking. Three metadata bugs the guards caught on the way: four calculator titles were over the REAL 46-char budget (60 minus the ' | GradeThread' suffix) because my own test used a bare 60; three descriptions were over 160; and the primary keyword 'clothing measurement converter' did not appear verbatim in the title, so the title became 'Clothing Measurement Converter and Size Chart'. CLOSED 2026-08-18 with the diagrams. Inline SVG, no image file: it survives the prerender, reads in both themes from currentColor with no hardcoded palette, and the labels are selectable text. The keys are compared against MEASUREMENT_HOWTO in the test, so a tenth measurement cannot be added without a line being drawn for it. One guard had to be corrected on the way: US-432 post-prerender check counts <title> elements and fails above one, which is right for a leaked Helmet title and wrong for an SVG accessible name -- it now strips SVG before counting, and measurement-diagram.test.tsx asserts the relaxation is exactly that narrow.

userStories.title: Fix the two underperforming comparison pages: poshmark-vs-mercari and depop-vs-poshmark
userStories.description: As a seller choosing where to list, I want a comparison that covers how each marketplace handles condition disputes and returns, so that I can pick on the terms that actually cost me money. CORRECTED 2026-08-18: this story originally asked to CREATE these two pages, on the claim that the comparison family held only mercari-vs-ebay. That claim came from grepping the COMPARISONS array in comparison-guides.ts, which holds one entry; the other 15 comparison routes are registered in public-routes.ts. Both pages have been live since 2026-07-06 with ~1,400 words each. The work is to fix them, not build them.
acceptanceCriteria: DIAGNOSED 2026-08-18, and the premise is wrong for the third time in this file. The pages are not the variable: which platforms they name is. All 16 comparison pages ship from one template on one publish date, and they split cleanly -- every pair naming Grailed or Vinted ranks in the top 15, every pair made only of eBay, Poshmark, Mercari and Depop ranks at 20 to 45. Full table and the two ruled-out confounds in docs/seo/compare-family-diagnosis.md.

Two alternatives ruled out rather than assumed. More words did not help: /compare/mercari-vs-ebay is the hand-written flagship and ranks 39th on 2 impressions, worse than 13 template pages. More internal links did not help: the only two pages carrying named anchor sets in interlink-rules.ts were poshmark-vs-mercari (44.8) and mercari-vs-ebay (39), so the confound runs backwards from the fix-the-page hypothesis.

DONE: the interlink anchor budget moved to /compare/vinted-vs-mercari (position 8.5) and /compare/grailed-vs-poshmark (position 11.0). Internal authority is worth spending where a page can cross a threshold into the top five, not on a page at 44.8.

DONE under US-9017: titles and meta descriptions rewritten for the four comparison pages that earn impressions. The other twelve keep the template, because there is nothing to learn from rewriting a page nobody sees.

VERIFIED IN CODE, not taken on trust from the note: the interlink anchor sets are on /compare/vinted-vs-mercari and /compare/grailed-vs-poshmark in interlink-rules.ts; the US-9017 rewrite for vinted-vs-mercari is in the worklist marked shipped; and the returns/condition-dispute row the story's description asks for already exists for all seven platforms in comparison-guides.ts, feeding a wedge row on every one of the 16 pages.

userStories.title: FlipDesk conversion landing pages for the high-bid commercial terms
userStories.description: As a seller who has just finished a fee calculation, I want a page that explains the tool that would do this automatically, so that I have somewhere to go other than back to the search results.
acceptanceCriteria: SUPERSEDED: one page per job-to-be-done for the five commercial terms. The diagnosis in AC2 said not to build them and the revised scope in AC7 replaced this. No new head-term landing page was built.

DIAGNOSED 2026-08-18 before writing anything. /reselling/best-crosslisting-apps IS the page this story proposed to build and it ranks 51.5 on 203 impressions, while every other crosslisting URL on the site ranks in the top 11. Full table in docs/seo/crosslisting-cluster-diagnosis.md.
These are judged on CONVERSION RATE, not search position. DONE: the funnel is instrumented and documented.

Each page has a single primary call to action into FlipDesk signup, and states the condition-grading differentiator that separates it from Vendoo and List Perfectly. DONE. /flipdesk/crosslisting gained a section that NAMES both competitors, concedes they cover more marketplaces, and argues the one axis where FlipDesk differs: they move your description between sites, they do not produce evidence about condition.

A PostHog funnel is defined from calculator view to landing page view to signup start, and registered in vault/40-growth/analytics-event-registry.md. DONE. commercial_landing_view fires on MOUNT rather than on a click, because a conversion rate needs its denominator; commercial_landing_signup_start on the primary CTA; crosslist_listicle_vendor_handoff on the listicle handoff, using the same {source, destination} pair as US-9018 and US-9006.
Registered in keyword-targets.ts. DONE for /flipdesk/crosslisting. It was already in the marketing sitemap segment via flipdeskLandingRoutes().

REVISED SCOPE ACTED ON: no second head-term landing page. Commercial intent now has a route to /flipdesk/crosslisting from the listicle, on a section that says plainly the listicle is not the place we argue for our own product.

THE LISTICLE STOPPED PRESENTING ITSELF AS NEUTRAL, which is the half of the trust problem a rewrite can actually fix. It called itself an 'honest roundup' with no disclosure that GradeThread builds one of the five tools it ranks. It now carries that disclosure above the fold, marks its own row in the at-a-glance table, and tells the reader to check the other four on their own sites.
The $34.51 top-of-page bid was treated as a warning, not a target, per AC8. Nothing was built for it.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN PASSING: US-9005's four fee calculators share one parameterised component, but ROUTE_PAGE_MODULES derives 'tools/{slug}', so four routes pointed at files that do not exist and their chunk preload silently did nothing (the US-1950 regression). The existing lockstep guard compares the KEYS of two maps built from one source, so it can only catch a typo. Calculator gained an optional pageModule, and src/test/route-page-modules-exist.test.ts now resolves every module id against the filesystem.
userStories.notes: Evidence added 2026-08-18 from the Search Console export. See docs/seo/unserved-query-clusters.md. Diagnosed 2026-08-18. The build this story asks for would have landed on page five next to the page that is already there.

userStories.title: Wire the calculators into the FlipDesk funnel and measure the handoff
userStories.description: As the operator, I want to know how many calculator visitors become signups, so that I can tell whether Path 3 is an acquisition channel or just traffic.
acceptanceCriteria: Every calculator page carries a contextual call to action into the matching FlipDesk surface, placed after the user has a result rather than before. DONE for all eight, rendered immediately above the FAQ block. MATCHED, not generic: fee calculators to /flipdesk/bookkeeping, the four marketplace ones to /flipdesk/crosslisting, the profit calculator to /flipdesk/comps, the measurement converter to /flipdesk/inventory-management. A test asserts at least three distinct surfaces, because if everything pointed at one page the per-calculator conversion rate would have nothing to distinguish.

PostHog events fire for calculator_used, calculator_cta_clicked and signup_started_from_tool, each carrying the calculator slug; all three are registered in vault/40-growth/analytics-event-registry.md. DONE, plus a FOURTH the story did not list and AC3 requires: calculator_view. Without the arrival count there is no denominator, and 'acquisition channel or just traffic' is a rate.

calculator_used is deliberately NOT a view. It fires once, on the first input change, so a visitor who read the Store-tier table and left can be told apart from one who typed their own numbers in. Those convert very differently and conflating them makes the rate meaningless.

ATTRIBUTION SURVIVES THE HOP, which is the part that would have quietly broken. The handoff goes to the matching /flipdesk/* page, not to /signup, so the calculator slug rides across in a `from` query parameter (TOOL_SOURCE_PARAM), the landing page reads it back, and signup_started_from_tool fires only when it is present. Without it every tool-driven signup would be credited to the landing page.

A dashboard or saved query reports calculator sessions, call-to-action click rate and signup conversion per calculator slug. DONE as far as it can be from here: all four query DEFINITIONS are written in vault/40-growth/analytics-event-registry.md. The dashboard itself is built in PostHog by hand and is operator work. Note the handoff rate is defined over USED rather than over VIEW, because the question is whether someone who got a result wants the product.

OPEN, DATED, NOT GUESSED: a baseline is recorded 30 days after the first calculator ships. The first shipped 2026-08-18 (US-9003), so the baseline is due 2026-09-17. It must not be invented before the window closes, because US-9016's kill criteria compare against it and a fabricated baseline makes them unfalsifiable. The date and the four rates to record are in the vault note.

7 tests in src/lib/seo/__tests__/calculator-funnel.test.ts: every live calculator has a handoff, every handoff points at a FlipDesk landing that exists, the surfaces are not all the same, the copy is not placeholder copy, and all four events are declared.

userStories.title: [GATE] SERP-check five repair terms before committing to the damage-and-care build
userStories.description: As the operator, I want to know who actually holds the top ten for the repair keywords, so that we do not commit to a 295,750/mo cluster that is locked up by domain-authority-80 incumbents.
acceptanceCriteria: Record the top ten organic results for the five terms. DONE, 2026-08-18, all five, 39 results recorded in docs/seo/repair-serp-check.md. Stated plainly in that note: this is a search-API sample, not a rank-tracker snapshot, so it answers WHO occupies the space and does not establish any URL's exact position.

For each, note how many of the ten are major publishers versus reachable sites, and whether any result is thin enough to displace. DONE. Across all 39 results there is EXACTLY ONE major publisher (Fox News, on an AMP real-estate URL). None of Tide, Persil, Good Housekeeping, Real Simple or Martha Stewart appears anywhere. The space is held by small craft blogs, clothing and appliance brand blogs, and UGC.

SIX OF 39 SLOTS ARE VISIBLY WEAK: a jewellery company ranking first for a sweater-snag query, Speed Queen's Thailand page for a US search, two spam PDFs on a hijacked New Zealand government domain, one more on a hijacked university domain, and a London waste-authority leaflet.
GATE RESULT: Path 1 is NOT blocked. AC3's kill condition is not met and it is not close. Path 1 is not recorded as blocked in the strategy note; the verdict and evidence are written into it instead.

Write the verdict and the evidence into the Path 1 section of the strategy note. DONE, in vault/40-growth/seo-strategy-options-2026-08.md, replacing the 'kill condition has not been tested yet' paragraph and reinforcing 'The risk Path 1 carries' with the same evidence.

THE FINDING THE STORY DID NOT ASK FOR, and it changes what Path 1 is worth rather than whether it is possible: not one of the 39 results is a resale, grading or secondhand-clothing site. The two closest are Oxfam, a charity shop, and Levi's. So there is no incumbent to displace, AND Google does not read these queries as resale-shaped and the visitor behind them is not a seller. The whole risk moves onto topical dilution.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE DOWNSTREAM STORIES, which is what a gate is for: US-9015 (containment) is reprioritised ahead of US-9013 and US-9014, because the boundary is cheap now and expensive after a hundred care pages exist. US-9013's entry terms are challenged in that story's own notes.

userStories.description: As someone with a broken zipper or a missing button, I want a step-by-step repair guide, so that I can fix the garment myself.

Build the repair sub-cluster before stain removal: repair is 122,000/mo across 10 terms with 8 on Low competition, where stain removal is 138,150/mo across 18 terms with 11 at Medium or High. Same volume, half the fight.
Each guide carries HowTo JSON-LD with real numbered steps, tools and materials, emitted from head-builder.ts as well as the SPA route.

Remaining repair terms (`how to fix a hole in jeans`, `how to fix a snag in a sweater`, `how to darn a hole in a sweater`, `how to replace a zipper pull`, `how to fix a stretched out collar`, `how to fix a broken belt loop`) are covered by the same template.

CHALLENGED BY THE US-9011 GATE (2026-08-18). This story names the two 50,000/mo terms as the entry point. The SERP check says enter on the 5,000/mo terms instead: `how to fix a snag in a sweater` and `how to unshrink clothes` have the weakest incumbents in the whole set (a jewellery site holds the top slot on the first; a wrong-locale appliance page and two spam PDFs hold three of seven slots on the second), and both are CONDITION DEFECTS WITH A RESALE CONSEQUENCE, which is the only bridge from repair intent back to the product.

DO NOT WRITE THE BUTTON PAGE YET. `how to sew on a button` is 50,000/mo of the purest non-adjacent intent in the set: someone searching it wants to sew a button, and the page-one results are craft blogs that do it better than we would. Volume is not the argument; adjacency is.

userStories.title: Flaw-crossed-with-fabric matrix, only where the answer genuinely differs
userStories.description: As someone with a specific stain on a specific fabric, I want advice for that combination, so that I do not ruin a silk blouse using a method written for denim.
acceptanceCriteria: A generated page family crossing the flaw taxonomy with the fabrics that behave differently, seeded from the existing fabric taxonomy rather than a new list.

A combination only gets a page when the procedure genuinely differs; combinations whose answer is identical to the parent flaw page are NOT generated and canonicalise to it instead. A test asserts no generated page duplicates its parent's procedure.
This is the test a programmatic family has to pass and the reason this one is allowed where Path 4's value pages were not: getting oil out of silk is not the procedure for cotton denim.
Page count is logged at build time so silent growth is visible; if the matrix exceeds 400 pages, the story stops and the cap is re-argued rather than shipped.
Every generated page is registered through calculatorRoutes()-style spread into PUBLIC_ROUTES and appears in the /care/ sitemap segment.

userStories.title: Containment guards so the care cluster cannot dilute the reseller entity
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the care content structurally separated from the reseller surface, so that Google's read of what GradeThread is does not drift toward laundry advice.
acceptanceCriteria: A test asserts no /care/ URL appears in the primary navigation, the homepage, or the top tier of functions/sitemap.xml.ts.

A test asserts the interlink rules in src/lib/seo/interlink-rules.ts allow /care/ pages to link INTO the reseller spine but not the reverse, so link equity flows toward the commercial pages and the entity signal does not invert.
Care content stays on the main domain in a subdirectory, NOT a subdomain: a subdomain would split the authority this cluster exists to build.
The ratio of care URLs to reseller URLs is reported by the sitemap build; the rationale for the chosen ceiling is recorded in vault/40-growth/seo-strategy-options-2026-08.md.

Path 1 is documented in the vault note as an authority and link engine, not an acquisition channel: it is 0.5% seller intent (1,550 of 295,750) and planning it as a customer channel is the failure mode this guard prevents.

userStories.title: Kill criteria and cluster tracking for the rebuilt SEO paths
userStories.description: As the operator, I want each new cluster measured against a threshold set in advance, so that the next review reads the numbers instead of rationalising them.
acceptanceCriteria: A Search Console cluster view per path (tools, compare, care, flipdesk-landing), one row each, extending the existing views in vault/40-growth/seo-distribution-and-measurement.md.

Thresholds set BEFORE the data arrives: Path 3 is failing if the calculator segment is under 2,000 impressions/mo at month 4; Path 1 is failing if the /care/ segment is under 10,000 impressions/mo at month 6; Path 7 is judged on signup conversion from tool traffic, not on impressions.

The depth test is recorded as a RATIO, not a count. The original 'thirty terms above 50/mo' rule measured how many terms got submitted rather than how deep the market is, and Path 3 could never have hit it on 23 submitted terms despite clearing volume six times over.
A quarterly re-pull of docs/seo/keyword-pull-2026-08.csv is scheduled so the bucketed figures (50/500/5k/50k) can be replaced with real numbers once the Ads account has spend.
The July 2026 grading-cluster kill criterion is marked as FIRED in the measurement note, since that is what triggered this rebuild.

userStories.title: Answer the migration intent on the comparison pages that already rank for it
